utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that and I cannot remember that there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: General, I thank you for your time and your candour and I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page of the document that we were just looking at, which is P2721, please. I apologise, Mr. Registrar, could we go to the next page. It's going to be 6757 will be the proper translation. Perfect. If we could have the -- could we have the portion which is the actually the body of -- of the document, where it starts "based on your consent." Yes, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just to clarify one matter, I believe this is your third page, it will be page 3 for you in B/C/S. Because there was some discussion for a moment about officers and discussion about members of the VTI, I'd just would like to get one understanding, which is, the gentleman who is in question here, Mr. Stojkovic, he is a civilian, right, and that's what the document says. It says: "Based on your consent," and it's confidential order number, and it says "civilian." Is that what that document says?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says that he was a highly qualified technician, repairman. That was his qualification, Mr. Stojkovic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to his qualifications, what he was highly qualified in --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have 6759 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which would be your page 5.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the text further on, namely that he was a sniper trainer, his qualification was that of a highly skilled technician. In the Military Technical Institute, they had equipment that was intended to adjust aims and he worked in a laboratory where they adjusted the aim on each individual piece of weaponry. After this was done, a certificate would be issued for each piece of weaponry, indicating how accurate it was in aiming, et cetera. And then this certificate would further on accompany that piece of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I'm wondering if you can help us here. It may be something that you know, it may not be something that you know, but are snipers as a class of soldier used in military operations?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, it is used. It exists routinely within units, primarily within infantry units.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you've mentioned and I believe that Ms. Carter actually read to you that the success of his training proved to be more efficient in combat operations. That's what he says in his report; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you had mentioned that because of his expertise one of the things that he was doing was he was helping with an understanding of -- technical understanding of how better to use the equipment, which resulted in less expenditure of ammunition; right? That's what the report says?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to legitimate military concerns, is a legitimate military concern the expenditure of ammunition within a combat operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army attempts to have the minimum use of not only ammunition but also other resources and they always try to carry out each task using minimum resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And of course, and unfortunate as it may be because it's a reality of war, the purpose of two sides fighting against each other and young men in the field with guns shooting is to hit, wound, kill, or disable the enemy; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as I understand his report, the training that he engaged in assisted in that occurring, which is a large number of hit soldiers on the enemy side, a military function; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were asked -- thank you so much for those answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'm done with this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were asked earlier about meetings, and I'm referring to page 26, line 19, in which there was a Mladic visit, and you had accompanied General Pustinja with General Mladic when you visited Crvena Zastava plant. Was General Perisic with you during that visit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to formation issues -- and by "formation issues" I mean documents that surrounded the formation of the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centre, a matter that you were discussing with Ms. Carter -- did you see any documents at that time dealing with the formation of the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I could have a moment, I need to just double-check something. Thank you, Mr. Kadijevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kadijevic, thank you so much. We've come to the end of your testimony. Thank you very much for taking the time off to come and testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused, you may stand down, and will you please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, are we coming back after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A slight change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir. Welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom and around it. The Defence is now ready to call its next witness, Mr. Rajko Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Welcome to you too, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. President, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Petrovic. You may take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Lukic. I'm sorry, Mr. Lukic. I've been with Mr. Guy-Smith for this week and his name is on my tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sudden changes in the course of one day. And this is the result.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rajko Petrovic

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, for the record, could you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is Rajko Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where were you born and when?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was born the 10th of March, 1964, in the village of Agarovici in the municipality of Rogatica in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please relax, sir. I don't know whether you are feeling relaxed enough in this position.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate your concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Second of all, I already told you during the proofing session that the two of us speak the same language and we have to have a clear record, therefore I would kindly ask you to wait a little after my question before giving your answer, and I will do the same after your answers. Could you please tell us, what is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm an officer in the army of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is the -- your current position in the army?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently I work in the sector for materiel assets of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is your rank in the army of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the army of Serbia I'm a lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is your establishment post, or rather, what rank is envisaged by your establishment post?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I will now swiftly go through your CV or some parts of your professional career which are of some relevance for these proceedings, in my opinion, and then we will focus on some parts of your professional biography as you provide your testimony. When did you graduate from the military academy and where was that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I graduated from the military academy of the land army in 1986 in Belgrade on the 26th of July. I became a 2nd lieutenant and my concentration was finances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other degrees or anything that would tell us something about your professional background?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also have a master's degree in military economic sciences and I obtained my master's degree at the military academy of the army of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you continued your education?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm currently working on my doctoral thesis, also at the military academy of the army of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now can you just briefly confirm the things that I will be reading from your personnel file. First of all, from February 1989, you were in the 639th Logistics Base of the then JNA of the 5th Military District in Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was the chief of finance of the 639th Logistics Base.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When the JNA withdrew from the territory of Croatia, on the 27th of February, 1992, pursuant to an order of the 2nd Military District of the then JNA you became a desk officer in the organ for planning and finances in the then 10th Corps of the 2nd Military District in the Bihac garrison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. When the Croatian army --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just give me a brief answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just briefly taking you through your career and then we will come back to some details thereof. Did there come a time when you became a member of a different military after the JNA; and if that was the case, when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became a member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 1st of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, what duties did you discharge from June 1992, and where did you serve?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was assigned to a position in the administration for the planning of development and financing of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, and I served in the -- in one of the departments and that was the department for planning and analysis. I was a desk officer for planning and analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How long did you remain a member of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained a member of the VRS up to April 1999, and then I became a member of the Army of Yugoslavia and that was in early April 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And since then, since April 1999 you have first been a member of the Army of Yugoslavia, and now --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And now I'm an officer in the army of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the period between 1992 and 1999 when you were an officer of the VRS, you told us where you served and did you discharge any other duties during that same period of time; and if you did, where was that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period I remained in the position that I mentioned up to January 1997, I believe. And then I remained in the same administration but I was appointed chief of department for control and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will discuss that administration in some more detail later on for everybody's benefit. And now tell us, what was your rank when you were a member of the VRS and did the rank ever change?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I joined the Main Staff of the VRS I was a captain. From January 1993 I was captain 1st class, and in that same month, January 1997, that is, I became a major.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who issued documents to upgrade you in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document on the interim promotion into captain 1st class was passed in January 1993 by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. I believe that the next document was also passed by him and that was confirmed by the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now let's go back to that same period in Bihac in 1992. That's the period I'm interested in. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said on page 55, line 12, the word that we use here in the courtroom, to verify, and verification, instead of "confirm," so the 30th Personnel Centre verified the appointment and in that sense I would like to intervene and correct the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I find it difficult to use the term "lieutenant-colonel" although we normally use ranks in this courtroom. Let me ask you this: Bihac 1992, you said what was your position was and what your duties were at that time. Did something happen in May 1992 that had an impact on your stay in Bihac?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1992 there were a few things, some of them more important than others, some of them had an impact on my further path. One of them was a telegram by General Blagoje Hadzic, who was acting on behalf of the federal secretary for defence, and in that telegram he informed all JNA members that a re-organisation of the JNA had already been underway and that JNA units had started withdrawing from the territories of the former republics of the SRJ into the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as well as the withdrawal of JNA members who were born in the territory of the SRJ as well as the need for those members and officers of the JNA to stay with the JNA in Bosnia-Herzegovina if they were born there. And that telegram was read to us by Colonel Grujo Boric after the previous commander of the 10th Corps of the JNA, General Nikovic, was pensioned off. After that, effectively Colonel Boric took over the command of the remainder of the command of the 10th Corps -- of the former 10th Corps. I apologise, I would also like to add that he said to us on that occasion that we should take decision according to our individual conscience and that he would not forbid anybody to leave, and that included even the officers who were born on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He also spoke about the pending establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska, the officers --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, let me interrupt you here. First of all, tell me this: After that, or later on when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, do you know what happened to Pukovnik Boric, what was his lot?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The remainder of the command of the former 10th Corps where I served as well, headed by Colonel Boric, were through, or rather, they left, and ended up in the territory near Drvar. The intention was to establish the command of the 2nd Krajina Corps, and its commander was Colonel Grujo Boric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After this telegram was read out to you, what was your reaction, Lieutenant-Colonel, and your decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My decision was the same as that of the other members of the JNA, namely that I should follow my conscience and naturally remain in Bosnia as a member of the Army of Republika Srpska which was being established. Its establishment was announced. I had no hesitation, no doubts even though in that telegram read out to us by Colonel Boric it said that the officers who remained in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina would be guaranteed certain status and certain benefits. There is nothing that could justify me leaving the area and allowing somebody else to defend my hearth while going to Belgrade myself, being an officer and all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said allowing somebody else to defend my?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, are you okay? Are you comfortable where you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does it look like I'm not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, naturally it's not pleasant to sit here. This is the first time I have ever testified before this court, and I spent a restless night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, if what I'm going to say is any comfort, let me just say it. Feel free. Nobody is going to do harm to you, nobody -- nothing will happen to you as a result of you talking and testifying in this court. Just relax, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember something about your colleagues from the unit who hailed from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina? How did they react to your decision to remain? And I would like to know how many of them remained and how many of them left, as far as you can remember.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, the majority of members of the JNA from that command remained. There were perhaps individual cases of people leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question, and we will now deal with the past, but it's all within the context. While you were in Zagreb and upon your arrival in Bihac, in that period of time, which was one year before the conflict erupted, the officers of other ethnicity - Muslims, Croats, Slovenians - did they also leave your unit during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There certainly were cases of people leaving. Almost all officers who were Croats or Slovenians left the unit. I even remember a major with whom we stood guard, he said to me, Rajko, I can no longer stand this. I will leave and you can shoot if you want. We kissed each other and he left the barracks, the barracks perimeter. I cannot remember his name just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your reaction to people leaving the unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood their decision. Their families were there and they almost had no other choice, had no other option.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you told us that starting on the 1st of June, 1992, you took up your new position in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I now orally amend our 65 ter list by showing to the witness a document marked 03388D. This is the document that Mr. Petrovic showed to me for the first time when we met on Saturday here in The Hague. I sent over to the OTP the B/C/S version of that document on the same day, on Saturday, and on the following day I sent them the draft translation, and if Ms. Carter agrees to this, I would ask that this document be shown to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objections to the oral amendment. The only concern that we have is if and when the document is actually tendered, that it be marked for identification so that our staff can have an opportunity to look over the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly intended to tender it in for -- to be marked for identification because we are still awaiting translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, before we turn to the document, tell us, how did you become member of the Army of Republika Srpska? Who informed you of that, where did you go, and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became a member of the Army of Republika Srpska by remaining there together with the portion of the former 10th Corps of the JNA, which had moved to Drvar and became the basis for establishing the command of the 2nd Krajina Corps. Shortly thereafter a telegram arrived from the Main Staff of the VRS, which had already been established. It first had the signature of General Djukic, and the Drvar command did not react to it. The second one came with the signature of General Mladic and it said that I was to report to my new duty at the Main Staff of the VRS urgently. I was to report to Han Pijesak and Crna Rijeka. Colonel Boric approved that and, after several days of travel, I reached Crna Rijeka. Shortly afterwards, they gave me the order on transfer and appointment, which we can see here, which was signed by the minister of defence of Republika Srpska, Colonel Bogdan Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document we can see that the number of this order is 21-1/92. It was issued on the 23rd of May, and can we see in this document what was the day you were appointed to this position?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, my appointment commenced on the 1st of June. A number of reports are written based on this order, hand-over of duty and so on. There are certain steps that need to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see something else here, which we will comment on later, establishment -- rank and establishment grouping; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please tell me what it says here. It says here duty -- what was your establishment position?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was acting clerk in the organ for planning and financial activity which, per establishment, was supposed to be, and was, major or lieutenant-colonel PG 14. However, given the rank I held at the time, I could not be appointed. Rather, they appointed me acting clerk, with my rank per establishment being captain 1st class, PG 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, a question concerning this organ where you worked, to which did it belong, this organ, organ for planning?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organ for planning was a part of the Main Staff which later grew into the administration for planning of development and financing. It was directly subordinate to the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who headed that administration?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This administration was headed by the then colonel and later on general, Stevan Tomic [phoen], general of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me this, please, what did this administration comprise? Which organisational units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administration had within its composition three organisational parts. It was a restrictive formation with a reduced number of personnel. They had the department for plan and analysis - that was the first department - the second one was for bookkeeping and records, and the third one was called regulations and control, or control and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many people worked in these three departments?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the restrictive establishment, there should have been a dozen or so people. However, there were only two men there; one was the chief of the administration, and I was the second one. I was a captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did somebody else come later on, somebody else who was your superior? I'm interested in --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't until mid-1993 that the department for plan and analysis where I worked got its chief, Colonel Vojin Matovic, who was at the same time deputy chief of the administration. For a period of time, it may have been six months in 1992 and in 1993, there was another officer who worked in the department for bookkeeping and records. However, he didn't stay there for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not manage to complete my previous question, so let me do it now. What you just described to us, is this how it was up until the end of the war, up until the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were just three men working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we MFI this document until we receive the official translation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D462, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, from the moment you joined the Army of Republika Srpska and when you started discharging all the different duties, what was your relationship with the Army of Yugoslavia? I am primarily interested in the status benefits.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to status benefits, we received salaries, and during that period of time there was no other benefit that I am aware of. And I'm talking about the early days, the initial period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was your number of pensionable years changed, did your health insurance change from the times when you were a JNA member?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any status entitlements with regard to your retirement benefits and health insurance benefits?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The same thing continued to be as it was in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will now deal with your salaries. How was your salary paid when you were a JNA member?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received salaries into our current accounts with the Postal Bank of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did there come a time when there were problems with the payment of salaries in Belgrade; and if that was the case, when?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was precisely during that period which was mid-1992. That period was very dynamic. There was interruption in the flow of payments and new currency was soon introduced. It was called dinar of Republika Srpska or the Republika Srpska dinar. I don't know what the tender was officially called. To put it simply, the situation was chaotic. It was very chaotic, actually. It started being chaotic already in Bihac. A lot of the ties were broken up or interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to be able to pursue the matter, I would firstly like to establish a certain basis for my next questions. When you joined the Main Staff and when you started working in your new position, did you have anything to do with the salaries in general and in particular the salaries of the troops of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The focus of my work in respect of the salaries was the payment of the Army of Republika Srpska. The funds were provided by the MOD of Republika Srpska, or rather, its government, the government of Republika Srpska. That was -- that concerned most of the personnel of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what were your activities with regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, at page 63, starting at line 1 -- sorry, not page 63, line 1. I thought earlier, and I may be wrong, I thought earlier you said that you were paid -- your salary was paid by the JNA. Now I think you are saying it was paid by the government of Republika Srpska. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the salaries of most of the VRS members were paid by the MOD of Republika Srpska. My salary, however, was paid in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, as it was already known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As well as the salaries of some other officers of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now, just briefly, could you please explain, what were your duties and tasks in respect of the payment of salaries funded from the budget of Republika Srpska via the MOD Republika Srpska? What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are we talking about? Are you talking about my responsibilities or my duties?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In my view it's almost the same. I see that they are not the same for you, so let me put it this way: What did you do with respect to the salaries?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were my obligations. My task was to collect information about the needs for funding, namely the salaries for corps units and units attached to the staff. Those needs depended on the current numerical strength in the corps. I prepared a document which was a request for funding. That document was signed by the commander of the Main Staff. And then that document, which was a request, would be forwarded to the MOD of Republika Srpska. Quite often, not to say always, it was sent to the president of the government. Shall I continue talking about the salaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm interested in this: If the funding was approved in respect of the salaries for those particular members of the Army of Republika Srpska who were funded from the RS budget, what would then be your activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My activities, once the funding was approved, were as follows: I was supposed to go and collect the money at an appropriate payment transactions office, and on that same day I distributed the money for the the corps and the staff, I followed and monitored the payment of salaries, and I requested from them to issue adequate documents for the payment of the salaries. And the document was the payroll signed by the members of the Army of Republika Srpska who received the salaries. From 1992, the funding came, the monies came into the sub-account of the Main Staff as well as the sub-accounts of the corps, and later on there was an account of the military computing [Realtime transcript read in error "competing"] centre of Banja Luka, or better say from the beginning of 2003 that happened. I apologise, 1993. I apologise for --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well, we will talk about that as well. Give me answers concrete questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you talk about the military computing centre in Banja Luka or competing centre? I thought you said computing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the title of the institution.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the military bookkeeping or computing centre of the Army of Republika Srpska in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll come to the second category of personnel, those who received salaries from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and I asked you a minute ago and you said that you had an account with the Postal Bank, you had a Postal savings account in Belgrade, and you said that there came a time when there were no longer monetary transaction flows between VRS and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. How was your salary paid after that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that period during which the monetary flows were interrupted -- actually, that period was rather painful. For a certain period of time or for awhile we used personal cheques that we had already raised with the Postal Bank and when it comes to companies in the territory of Republika Srpska, we exchanged those personal cheques for the commodities that they purchased from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and then they used our cheques to effectuate payment for the goods that they purchased from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you also receive cash independently of the Postal Bank; and if that was the case, who was it who raised that cash?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that on one occasion I went to the bookkeeping centre of the MOD of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and I signed a receipt against which I was issued a negligible amount of money which was also used for the payment of salaries. The payments were effectuated in a very restricted fashion. Cheques were obtained from the Postal Banks and those cheques were then taken to the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence, and the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence then sent them to the Postal Bank and exchanged them for cash against a debt note, debt certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was that, during what period of time? Could you tell us the year? You don't have to be more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was in 1992. After that, the current accounts were blocked, sometime in July and August. I'm talking about the initial period of 1992, about early 1992. Actually, not early 1992 but June and July. That was just after the Army of Republika Srpska was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And later on was the payment transaction flow restored? Could you then be paid through the Postal Bank?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Postal -- the payment transactions between Republika Srpska and the FRY were never reinstated, but as far as I can remember, sometime in September, October an agreement was reached at a certain level with the Postal Bank, and according to that agreement, payments could be made into the Postal Bank by the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And those payments would be made based on the lists certified in the corps or the staff or some other organisational unit of the Army of Republika Srpska. And then such monies could be withdrawn depending on the situation with the cash at the Postal Bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How important was it for you to physically receive the salary as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, during 1993 and 1992, when the rate of inflation was exorbitant, by the time we received the salaries from Belgrade, by the time we received money from Belgrade, that money had completely lost its value. It had been completely devalued. So much so that very often you couldn't even buy ten packs of cigarettes. I believe there was a brand called Vek that cost 2.5 marks, and we couldn't even buy that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the proofing sessions you showed me a bank note that you have kept. How many zeros were on it, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I have it still. I'm looking at it. I don't want to make a mistake. This is a bank note of 50 billion dinars. It was issued in late 1993. The year is 1993. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let's be economical and use the opportunity to show everybody in the courtroom the bank note that you are holding in your hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, just put it on there. When was this bank note issued?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the later half of 1993, as far as I can remember. If I may continue, I don't think you could buy a sandwich for this note. There was another bank note which was the 500 billion one. I don't have it and, as far as I know, that note was the highest denomination ever printed anywhere in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just state for the record that this note that we can see on the ELMO contains figure 5 and ten zeros. I'm unable to describe it verbally. Your Honours, I will perhaps scan this note and then on Friday I will perhaps tender it, but for the time being I will make no requests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now, Your Honours, use a document of the same form as the previous document. By your leave, I would like to orally amend our 65 ter list with the document 03389D 65 ter. Once again this is a document that Mr. Petrovic gave to me during proofing and which I disclosed to the OTP as soon as I received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Under the same guise as the last one, we just ask for it to be marked as MFI so we can look at the translation, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document to be put on the screen, Mr. Petrovic, you see that this is the document by way of which you were promoted, the promotion enactment. We already heard some testimony before this Court, but if you can tell us in one sentence, what elements does a salary of an officer contain?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main element was determined by the rank and the other main element was determined by the position to which one was appointed. And then other elements of the salary were calculated based on these two basic elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you describe this document to us.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the order on my extraordinary promotion to the rank of captain 1st class in the financial services. This document was issued and signed by the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It says that as of the 7th January 1993, I was being promoted to the rank of captain 1st class.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we just look at something. The number of this order is 28/17-1 and the date is 7 January 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 7th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we mark this document for identification as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D463 marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now the next document I would like us to look at, Your Honours, is once again a document we received from the OTP in the financial file of this witness, and in our 65 ter list this is 0401D. Again we are still awaiting the official translation. In the meantime, we can use the draft translation if Ms. Carter agrees, then we can discuss it with the witness and propose that it be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: That seems the appropriate reaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Just for brief clarity of the record, actually this is from the financial file, not the personnel file. I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. And I think that I did say the financial file. If I made a mistake, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Petrovic, please tell us what is this that we see before us?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a record of monetary data which is kept in the accounting centre in relation to each person to whom a salary is paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now zoom in, Your Honours, the upper right corner where the blue stamp is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could the witness tell us whose stamp this is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the stamp of the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence Belgrade. They calculated and paid out salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says here "VP 7572 Sarajevo." Whose VP is this, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This military post is the military post of the Army of Republika Srpska where I served, that is to say, the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move to the left part of the document, the lower portion, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In window number 4, could we look at that. This box 4, what kind of data is entered there, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4, box 4, where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, the Roman IV. It's on the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. The data concerning on salary grade is entered here based on the appointment that an officer holds. As I have already said, this element of the salary makes up the basic salary to which other percentages are added. This is the position element, and we also have the rank element.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: The last column within this box, it says here "acting clerk."

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "acting clerk in the organ for planning of the Main Staff of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," as Republika Srpska was called initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This number, 21-1/92, what does it stand for, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the order on appointment. The number of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the document that we saw just a minute ago, signed by Mr. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And to the right we see the date, the 1st of June, 1992. What does this date stand for?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That date is the date when I took over the duties of that clerk in the organ for planning of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 13 PG, what does that signify?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the number based on which salary is calculated. Salary grades carried a certain amount of points.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then underneath it, it says "Clerk at the GLST" again 13. The date is the 7 of February 1994, which is the date of the order, there is the number of the order, and the date of appointment is the 10th of November, 1993. Does that mean anything to you, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the promotion to the rank of captain 1st class -- it says 7th of February, 1994, yes. So after being promoted to the rank of captain 1st class, I met the conditions for being appointed to the position of clerk so that I was no longer acting clerk but became clerk. I was appointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you could look at your screen and confirm that we are all looking at the same page. I'm looking for the 7th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, underneath the box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Petrovic: We will discuss this at length tomorrow, but did you ever hear of the 30th Personnel Centre and do you know when it was established?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA KADIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear of the 30th Personnel Centre, and as far as I remember, it was established in the later half of 1993, September or so. I'm not sure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as not to forget, could this document be MFI'd and I will look at this document again tomorrow -- rather, the day after tomorrow with this witness. Otherwise, we can conclude for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D464 marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Petrovic, we are not done with you. We'll come back on Friday because tomorrow we are not working. On Friday at 9.00 in the morning, but in the meantime while you were still testifying you are not allowed to talk to anybody about this case, and in particular not members of the Defence team. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Then the court stands adjourned to Friday morning at 9.00 in Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.
